call_function.description: Run one of your project's database functions and get back what it returns. A function can change or delete data as well as read it, so check what it does before you use it here.
call_function.name: call_function

parameters.description: The function's name as it is in your database, such as get_open_orders. It must be in the public schema.
parameters.name: function

parameters.description: The function's inputs by name, given as name-and-value pairs (for example, {"customer_id": 42}). Leave blank for a function that takes none.
parameters.name: arguments

result.description: What the function returned: a value, a row, or a list of rows.

delete_rows.description: Permanently delete every row in a Supabase table that matches your conditions. Deleted rows can't be brought back.
delete_rows.name: delete_rows

parameters.description: The name of the table to delete rows from.
parameters.name: table

parameters.description: Only delete rows where these columns exactly equal these values, given as column-and-value pairs (for example, {"id": 42}).
parameters.name: match

insert_row.description: Insert a new row into a Supabase table.
insert_row.name: insert_row

parameters.description: The name of the table to add the row to.
parameters.name: table

parameters.description: The new row's columns and values. Pick a table and its columns appear as fields to fill in; if the table comes from an earlier step, enter column-and-value pairs yourself (for example, {"name": "Ada", "email": "ada@example.com"}).
parameters.name: row

list_rows.description: Get rows from a Supabase table, with optional filters to narrow the results.
list_rows.name: list_rows

parameters.description: The name of the table to read from.
parameters.name: table

parameters.description: The columns to return. Pick from the table's columns; leave empty to return every column.
parameters.name: columns

parameters.description: Only return rows where these columns exactly equal these values, given as column-and-value pairs (for example, {"status": "active"}). Leave blank to return every row.
parameters.name: match

parameters.description: The most rows to return. Leave blank to return all matching rows.
parameters.name: limit

update_rows.description: Update every row in a Supabase table that matches your conditions. The columns you give replace the values already there.
update_rows.name: update_rows

parameters.description: The name of the table to update.
parameters.name: table

parameters.description: Only update rows where these columns exactly equal these values, given as column-and-value pairs (for example, {"id": 42}).
parameters.name: match

parameters.description: The columns to change and their new values, given as column-and-value pairs (for example, {"status": "done"}).
parameters.name: updates

rows.description: The rows that were updated, with their new values.

upsert_row.description: Add a row to a Supabase table, or, if a row with the same key is already there, overwrite that row's columns with the values you give. Columns you leave out keep their values.
upsert_row.display_str_template: Insert or update a row in '{table}'.
upsert_row.name: upsert_row

parameters.description: The name of the table to save the row in.
parameters.name: table

parameters.description: The row's columns and values, including the ones that identify it. Pick a table and its columns appear as fields to fill in; if the table comes from an earlier step, enter column-and-value pairs yourself (for example, {"id": 42, "status": "paid"}).
parameters.name: row

parameters.description: The columns that say whether the row is already there, such as email. They must be the table's primary key or have a unique constraint. Leave empty to use the primary key.
parameters.name: match_columns

row.description: The row as it is now saved.

description: List, insert, update, and delete rows in your Supabase tables, call database functions, and start a workflow when a row is added.

supabase_new_row_trigger.description: Runs when a row is added to a Supabase table, found by checking for rows past the highest id (or other ever-growing column) seen so far. Rows already in the table don't trigger it.

parameters.description: The table to watch, e.g. orders.
parameters.name: table

parameters.description: A column whose value grows with every new row, such as an auto-increment id or a created-at time. Leave blank to use the table's primary key.
parameters.name: column
